articleTitle: Prediction of the Effect of Electrical Defibrillation Based on the Wavelet Transform with Pseudo-Differential Operators
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This paper proposes a prediction system of the effect of electrical defibrillation based on the wavelet transform with pseudo-differential operators. To construct this system first, we analyze and extract features from pre-shock (before defibrillation) ECGs (ElectroCardioGrams) by using Gabor wavelet transform with pseudo-differential operators. Next, the effective feature parameters are selected based on the χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> test. Finally, this system predicts two states such as "Effective" and "Ineffective" defibrillation by using the SVM (Support Vector Machine). In this way, we show the effectiveness of the proposed feature extraction method and prediction system.

articleTitle: A study on the Probabilistic EV Load Model for Distribution Planning and the Contribution of Power System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: With the global expansion of electric vehicle (EV) adoption, an increase in electricity demand is expected. In South Korea, EV penetration continues to rise, particularly on Jeju Island, where efforts are being made to increase EV adoption in order to achieve the "Carbon Free Island Jeju 2030" goal as outlined in the "4th Comprehensive Plan for Electric Vehicles." This paper explores the probabilistic prediction of EV charging load and investigates the use of the recently introduced Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology, which utilizes EV batteries as Energy Storage Systems (ESS), to ensure a stable power supply. In terms of probabilistic analysis, charging data from nationwide EV charging stations, categorized by season and weekdays/weekends, were used to divide charging amounts into intervals based on the binomial distribution. The average charging amount for each interval was calculated and weighted accordingly to predict charging amounts probabilistically. The predicted charging amounts for each time period were verified to closely match the actual charging amounts using MSE (Mean Squared Error). By utilizing EV batteries with such capacity as ESS, connecting idle or charging EVs nationwide to the power grid could contribute to the stable operation of uncertain renewable energy sources and help stabilize the power grid frequency accordingly.

articleTitle: LMI-Based Non-Iterative Design Strategies for Guaranteed Cost Static Output Feedback Control for Linear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This paper proposes a non-iterative LMI-based design strategy for guaranteed cost static output feedback controllers for linear systems. The proposed design approach is based on the well-known necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of the static output feedback stabilizing control for linear systems. In this paper, for linear systems we show the non-iterative LMI-based design procedure for static output feedback controllers which minimize the upper bound of a given quadratic cost function, and the effectiveness of the proposed static output feedback controller with guaranteed cost is presented through a simple numerical example.

articleTitle: Comparison of Control Strategies for AC/DC Converter for a Wind Energy System with Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Wind energy contributes to diversifying the energy matrix. These systems can be adapted to various scales, from industrial wind farms to smaller residential systems, makingaccessible and versatile. Furthermore, wind systems promotes environmental preservation by reducing dependence on nonrenewable energy sources like fossil fuels, significantly contributing to climate change mitigation. The challenge posed by wind energy lies in controlling it against disturbances with high variability, such as wind speed. To address this challenge, advanced control systems must be implemented to optimize the performance of wind turbines and minimize the adverse effects of varying wind conditions. This work presents the design and implementation of two control strategies for the AC/DC converter of a wind system with a PMSG generator. First a traditional PI controller is used, followed by a PI+Fuzzy-PI controller. The aim is to analyze and compare the dynamic performance of both control techniques. The results show that the PI+Zuzzy-PI controller has a better dynamic performance than PI controller. The overshoot and settling time can be reduced in the former. Therefore, the effectiveness of PI+Fuzzy –PI controller is evaluated and demonstraed.

articleTitle: Road Corner Detection System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Taking comer in a vehicle on the road might be dangerous when it is done at a high speed as it might cause one to lose control of the car. Sometimes, the driver loses attention while driving due to many reasons that can be harmful to them, and the worst of them is an accident. This unwanted event has to be paid attention to since accident cases around the globe are increasing from day to day, and need an urgent solution to reduce or at least slow down the expanding percentage of accident cases. This project aims to improve the safety features of a car by developing a system that can detect comer when a car is approaching it and process the data collected to take precautionary steps in avoiding accidents. This system will discover the comer by reading the line lane on the road. A proper algorithm will be. developed using Python, with the assistance of OpenCV and NumPy libraries. This algorithm will be simulated using pre-recorded video, to make the development process more manageable and improvements can be applied directly to the system.

articleTitle: Torque-Controlled DC Motor for Wind Turbine Simulator Application
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Wind turbine simulator (WTS) has been widely used to enhance research flexibility in the field of power electronics for maximum power point tracking (MPPT). This WTS consists of a DC motor and a buck chopper that are used for simulating the wind turbine characteristics. The DC motor is controlled by using the proportional integral (PI) controller to follow the scaled wind turbine torque reference or equivalent torque. A 200 W DC motor, LVDAC-EMS software, MATLAB Simulink, and Arduino UNO are used to implement the proposed system. The results show that the wind turbine simulator can produce torque output that follows the equivalent torque reference at wind speeds of 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10 m/s, with relative root mean square error (RRMSE) values of 8.8%, 5%, 4%, 3%, 3%, and 4% respectively. The lowest RRMSE occurs at wind speeds of 8 and 9 m/s, while the highest at 5 m/s. The highest RRMSE at low wind speeds occurs due to the vibration on the rotor.

articleTitle: A Simulation Study of the Impact of Air Conditioning Control System Design on Energy Efficiency Towards Net-Zero Energy Buildings
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The Malaysian government is encouraging the industry players to have more awareness of sustainable energy and energy efficient building practices. As the impact, achieving Net-Zero Energy Buildings (NZEB) has become popular among researchers. NZEB can be achieved by integrating renewable energy systems such as solar photovoltaic into the building. Another factor contributing to the energy performance of buildings is the design and implementation of the cooling system in the building. However, upgrading a conventional building to NZEB is a challenge. As an example, an air conditioning system is one of the complexities towards achieving recognition as energy efficient buildings. The paper investigates the impact of air conditioning with conventional control system designs on energy consumption in a building. The system is modelled using Simulink by integrating the air conditioning system model into a building system model where it is based on Malaysia weather. The system compares the conventional control system of the compressor’s limit range. The results show that a lower limit range dissipates more heat compared to a higher limit range. For future work, it is suggested to apply inverter control for the air-conditioning system.

articleTitle: Gaze Estimation Using VGG16 Architecture Through XGBoost Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Gaze Estimation, a technology that has evolved in the modern era that revolves around analysing the movement of eyes and their patterns which covers a wide array of fields and domains. It transformed human-computer interaction by providing hands-free device control and navigation through visual focus. In this study, an unique approach has been introduced for estimating the gazes of the eyes through VGG16 model by modifying it’s architecture that preserves it’s base layers but replacing the softmax layer with an XGBoost classifier for better classification. For estimating it’s efficiency, a comparative analysis has been conducted with various deep learning architectures. Through the implementation of the architecture, the primary aim is to outperform the benchmark models with notable performance improvements. The outcomes are highly encouraging and the modified architecture provides more precise estimation of gazes than the benchmark models.

articleTitle: Balancing the Capacitor Voltage Drift in Neutral Point Clamped Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: It is common for 3-level Neutral Point Clamped (NPC) bridges to incorporate a capacitive voltage divider on their DC side. When the two capacitors are identical, the total DC voltage is evenly distributed between them. However, in practice, without corrective measures, the DC capacitor voltages deviate from their nominal values as soon as the system starts exchanging power. This voltage drift occurs during both steady state and transient conditions. Balanced DC voltages are crucial for the proper functioning of the NPC converter, which is why various methods have been proposed in the literature to address the voltage drift problem. In this study, we present a different solution to the capacitor voltage drift problem that does not need any external hardware, and instead uses the switch modulating waveforms to correct the voltages. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated by time domain simulations on an active front end converter that exchanges variable amounts of active and reactive powers with the grid.

Author Keywords: Capacitor Voltage Drifting in NPC Converters

articleTitle: Design and Improved performance of High gain Wearable Textile Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In recent years, the development and utilization of wearable antennas has grown rapidly and one of the challenging improvements is wearable textile antenna. The significance of wearable antennas is, they are designed as elements of clothing which is capable to transmit or receive wireless signals. Properties of the textile antenna such as bandwidth, efficiency, input impedance etc. mainly depends on the type of substrate materials used. The Literature survey has been done for various wearable antennas in an extensive way. The existing antennas are made up of artificial magnetic conductor as a ground plane. This paper focuses on design and analysis of wearable textile antenna. Two antenna structures are designed and its performances are analyzed through simulation. One of the proposed antennas is fabricated using jean as a substrate with the length of 45mm, width of 45mm, bandwidth of 512MHz and with a gain of 9.32dBi. The proposed antenna operates within the ISM band of 5.8GHz. It is used in health monitoring, emergency rescue, military etc. The Proposed antenna structure is fabricated and its performances are tested for various parameters and compared. It is observed that proposed antenna has better improvement in gain and has large bandwidth of 590 MHz. Moreover, the proposed antenna is made up of jean; it provides a very high compatibility and flexibility compared to other wearable antennas.

articleTitle: Modified Blood Oxygen Levels Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: A gadget called an OXIMETER is used to measure blood oxygen levels. The oximeter does not produce correct results in people with scleroderma, those who have decreased tissue perfusion, such as is the case in anemia instances, and people who have digital ulcers. Scleroderma is an autoimmune illness in which the body attacks its own cells because it believes they are foreign invaders, making the skin rough and making it difficult to accurately measure blood oxygen levels. OXILASER is a gadget that combines an oximeter and a laser. The laser aids in penetrating through rough skin to easily and accurately measure blood oxygen levels.

articleTitle: A review of Low-Power Energy Harvesting technologies in Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Nowadays, in the modern world, wireless electronic devices or those with wireless capabilities are significantly popular because there is no need for them to obtain any power connections to the main grid. As a result, batteries are now playing the main role in supplying power for electronic devices for household use or industrial use, making wire connection becomes the choice for battery charging purposes only. Battery manufacturing technology has made a huge step in improving battery life but still requires frequent maintenance which causes a big gap between battery life and the need of the users. Furthermore, recycling the depleted batteries after use is quite challenging despite many efforts being put into research for solutions to this matter. Even though some solutions were introduced as eco-friendly ones, their recycling problems are still in doubt, for example, recycling the PV panels or recycling the Lithium batteries from electric vehicles is still a headache for scientists. As it is now the trend of using "green electronics", it would be not a good approach to rely so much on the grid power supply. Energy has to be collected through the surrounding activities with the reduction of using Copper or wire in power transfer. There have been many scientific researchers who were interested in tackling this problem and they spent a lot of effort in researching energy harvesting technologies. As a result, different aspects of battery life and energy harvesting study have been taken into research, such as battery charging efficiency, energy collector efficiency, power converter efficiency, etc. For Industry 4.0, low-power energy harvesting is highly needed as the small sensors or small power modules will be leveraged by this kind of technology. This paper aims to examine the current state of knowledge on low-power energy harvesting technology, including its benefits, limitations, and future potential.

articleTitle: Securing the Smart Grid: A Comprehensive Analysis of Recent Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Cyber security is the entire process of stopping attackers from using information asset weaknesses to compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets. Therefore, the three main components of cybersecurity—confidentiality, integrity, and availability—must be appropriately provided. The dangers and attacks related to cyber security are one of the main issues with constructing the vital infrastructures of today. The primary component of vital infrastructures, electrical energy is produced, transmitted, and distributed in a way that is efficient using smart grids. The growing usage of smart grids necessitates the identification and classification of dangers as well as the implementation of countermeasures. Smart grids must have the most advanced information security since they are at least minimally vulnerable to cyberattacks. In this context, this paper introduces several attack types, assaults on smart grids, and significant cyber-attacks on power systems. Additionally, the primary goals and specifications for cybersecurity in smart grids are provided. Moreover, the concepts of confidentiality, integrity, and availability are used to categorize the many attack types that can be used in smart grids. The study is then assessed.

articleTitle: Newly-Designed DC-Arc Fault Detection Strategy Via EMD Signal Analysis and GRU Neural Network for Solar PV Power Generation System
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: In this study, an intelligent arc-fault detection algorithm for solar photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems is investigated based on the empirical mode decomposition (EMD) and the gate recurrent unit neural network (GRU-NN). The proposed algorithm uses the EMD to extract valuable information from current signals and then sequences the statistical indexes of each mode from the EMD according to modal orders. Moreover, the GRU-NN captures the features and variation trends among different modes and eventually detects the dc-arc fault. Through experimental verifications, the average detection accuracy is over 98.7%, with an 8ms execution time under all examined conditions. In addition, an online updating method is also introduced in this study to ensure the adaptability of the proposed algorithm. Combined with this online-updating method, the proposed EMD-GRU-NN scheme could quickly modify the model and ensure the accuracy of the arc fault identification, even for different PV stations. The online updating performance will also be verified by experiments in Taiwan and China PV stations to improve over 25% detection accuracy to previous research.

articleTitle: Smartphone-Based Technique for Disease Detection through Finger Nail using Fractal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: There is an increased need for Point-Of-Care (POC) devices since it is challenging to diagnose some diseases in resource-constrained areas. In medical science, professionals meticulously examine the patient's nails to gather important information about their health. Since the human eye is limited in its ability to distinguish between colors, shapes, and textures, digital image processing techniques are employed to assess the condition of the nails to diagnose human health. An important area of the healthcare domain nowadays is non-invasive disease diagnostics. In this work, a patient's fingernail is used to diagnose their medical issues. The major goal of this research is to use a computational platform to immediately diagnose disease from a patient's fingernail without administering any medications. To gather datasets, an image-capturing device has been created. The nail is then evaluated using the fractal dimension technique to look for any disorders. This work aims to give an analysis based on fractals. As fractal theory is based on calculating the roughness of the surface, it can be applied to fingernails. The texture of healthy nails is observed to be smooth and unhealthy nails have a rough texture. The fractal values of healthy nails based on different age groups and different occupational groups using two fractal dimension approaches based on the spatial domain, i.e. box-counting method, and frequency domain, i.e. Fourier fractal dimension method is calculated, and then the liver-diseased nails are compared with healthy nails and analysis is done. For all groups of healthy nails, the fractal value is computed between 1.3 and 1.79, while for nails with liver disease, it is calculated between 1.81 and 1.84 for box-counting dimensions. The fractal value for the Fourier fractal dimension is estimated between 0.013 and 0.034 for healthy nails, while for nails with liver disease, it is computed between 0.058 and 0.066. As a result, this work is used to identify a disease from fingernails. This method is completely noninvasive. Additionally, it resolves the problem of costly facilities not being affordable in remote regions.

articleTitle: Selecting Sampling Based Planners for Local Planning in Unpredictable Environment for a Six-Axis Robot Manipulator
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: One of the solutions to planning in a changing environment involves two stages: global planning and local planning. This paper attempts to select a group of sampling-based planners for planning in a dynamic environment workspace for local planning according to the performance statistics of geometric sampling-based planners in a changing environment with unpredictable static objects. The planners are evaluated in a workspace with unpredictable static obstacles. The planners discern collision-free motion planning for a six-axis robot arm in changing environment. The robot arm has an eye-in-hand perception unit, the Realsense RGB-D camera, to model the surrounding. A static obstacle is introduced at random location at random time step in the workspace to emulate the changing environment in a work cell of an automation floor. The planners are subjected to an improved inverse-kinematic solver using a numerical method, the Newton-Raphson with sampling constraints, to facilitate online planning and replanning. The constraints are defined in the task space. The performance statistics are compiled for twenty four planners. In this paper, eleven planners are shown to reliably produce collision-free solutions at processing time of less than 0.1 seconds.

articleTitle: Power Quality Disturbance Feature Extraction And Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Poor quality of power supplies could have the potential to interfere with communication networks, increase power losses, reduce life periods of electrical/electronic equipment, and cause a variety of malfunctions in power generation, transmission, distribution, and in end-users’ systems. Therefore, it is imperative to ascertain what power quality (PQ) problems the electricity grids are currently suffering and what are the formats and occurring frequencies of them, and then find out necessary countermeasures to mitigate the impacts they have been bringing about. Apparently, techniques of effective feature extraction and accurate classification are essential for the PQ disturbance recognition required by a smart grid. In the paper, after comparing some main feature extraction approaches, the authors present a PQ disturbance recognition scheme based on the combination of support vector machines and error correcting output codes. With the proposed feature extraction using Fourier and wavelet transforms respectively, the performance of the designed recognition system is verified. Simulations have shown that the proposed recognition methods, in particular when using the Fourier transform, can achieve superior performance in terms of simplicity of feature extraction and high accuracy of the classification.

articleTitle: Profiling Wiper Arm Surface for Appearance Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Defect detection in the wiper arm manufacturing industry is not highly automated due to the task complexity. In addition to its non-uniform structure, a wiper arm is usually dark and has a reflective surface. Prior work on area scan camera showed images with narrow visible zones and small regions of interests (ROI). Consequently, a lot of sequential images need to be taken consecutively and processed. Despite many effort to improve its performance using various image processing techniques, the defects that occur at the boundary of the ROI were not detected as they blended into the background during binarization. This paper proposed to use a line scan camera to capture images that resulted in a much wider visible zone. The total number of images to be captured per wiper arm has significantly reduced from 66 to 10. The image processing time per wiper arm has also improved tremendously from 7.45 seconds to 0.067 seconds. With considerable decrease in the miss-detection of this type of defects, the overall accuracy has improved from 0.905 to 0.935. Meanwhile, the classification accuracy for scratch, bump and dent is 86.16%, 97.06% and 98.02% respectively. This shows that a line scan camera performs better in this application, even though the set-up is more complicated.

articleTitle: Smart Biofloc System: Leveraging IoT for Enhanced Aquaculture Sustainability
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative solution to address a critical issue in Biofloc aquaculture systems: water quality management. In Biofloc technology maintaining optimal water quality is crucial for the quantity and quality of fish production. For this we've developed an IoT-based system with carefully calibrated sensors that collect continuous data on essential parameters: temperature, Dissolved Oxygen (DO), pH, water level, turbidity, and Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) from the Biofloc environment. Each sensor was meticulously calibrated and tested against commercially available devices. The temperature sensor exhibited a Mean Squared Error of 0.0042, while the DO and TDS sensors had average errors of 2.45% and 4.30%, respectively. The pH sensor performed perfectly compared to the commercial device, but the turbidity sensor couldn't be evaluated due to a lack of a suitable measurement device. The collected data is transmitted to a cloud server for rigorous processing, allowing real-time assessment and analysis. The system includes actuators that autonomously adjust key parameters, such as temperature, DO, and pH, to maintain optimal water quality. We use a heater, air pump, and acidalkaline solutions to manage water quality, while a water pump and integrated automated drainage system maintain the optimal water level. In case of parameter abnormalities, the system promptly notifies the user. To provide users with instant insights and control, we've developed a user-friendly mobile application offering real-time monitoring and adjustment capabilities. Through this innovative approach, our IoT-based Smart Biofloc Monitoring and Maintenance System aims to significantly enhance the efficiency, sustainability, and overall success of Biofloc aquaculture practices.

articleTitle: Space-Vector D-STATCOM System for Power Quality Correction in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Custom power devices (CPD) are the present trend for power quality correction in distribution networks. This paper deals with one such mechanism, namely, the distribution static synchronous compensator (D- STATCOM). The proposed device is used for voltage swell/sag compensation in a test case distribution system using a space vector-based switching technique. The voltage sag is often observed in the presence of R-L, R-L-E, and other non-linear loads. On the other hand, a voltage swell is caused by the R-C loads. The placement of D-STATCOM for power factor amelioration is also considered. The vector control technique’s applicability is to enhance the power factor of the entities. The vector control technique independently administers the active power as well as the reactive power. The validation of the proposed technique is done with the help of simulation results using SIMULINK/MATLAB.

articleTitle: Environmental Assessment on the Effect of Particulate Matter as Air Pollutant to the Health of Individuals in Ermita, City of Manila, Philippines
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: During the course of the study, the researchers were able to monitor the quality of air in the areas of Ermita, Manila via the monitoring station in Mehan Garden in Ermita, Manila using the real-time monitoring of AccuWeather and the DENR-EMB. Based on the findings, there has been a decline in Particulate Matter 2.5 (PM2.5) over the years, the Particulate Matter 10 (PM10) and TSP abides the target levels suggested by the Clean Air Act. The monitored data available for Manila majority falls under Interim Target #4, where the target concentration for PM2.5 is 25 microgram/Nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> annual-mean. Nevertheless, it exceeds the World Health Organization's Air Quality Guideline for PM2.5 where 15 microgram/ Nm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is the target. Apart from this, the researchers also performed a survey of random people on the area surrounding the research locale, which is Mehan Garden, Ermita, Manila. The researchers were able to conclude from this that the respondents' most common comorbidities were diseases, notably lung conditions like asthma, which makes air pollution related to these types of diseases. At the end of the research, the researchers proposed interventions that can address the concern.

articleTitle: Comparative Study to Identify Requirement Issues to Build Low Cost Solar System For Sri Lanka A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: Due to the rising need for energy and the tropical location of Sri Lanka, solar power has emerged as an appealing alternative source of electricity in the Sri Lanka. As a direct result of the current state of the economy, we are seeing an ongoing rise in the amount that we are required to pay for power daily. However, the high cost of solar systems continues to be a significant barrier for a significant number of companies and homes. This review article seeks to give a comparison research on identifying necessary difficulties to create low-cost solar systems and yet existing systems for Sri Lanka. The study will be provided as a comparative analysis. The study provides an overview of the previous research that has been conducted on the subject and conducts an analysis of the numerous elements that impact the cost of solar systems. These aspects include the efficiency of solar panels, storage systems, and regulatory laws. Additionally, case studies and actions conducted by a variety of organizations to promote low-cost solar systems in Sri Lanka are analysed and discussed in this study. The conclusions of this review study will give a better knowledge of the required challenges for creating low-cost solar systems in Sri Lanka. This understanding will be beneficial for policymakers, researchers, and enterprises in the energy industry.

articleTitle: From Monolith to Service-Oriented Architecture: A Model-Based Design Approach towards Software-Defined Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 5th International Conference on Electrical, Control and Instrumentation Engineering (ICECIE)
abstract: The automotive industry has exhibited great limberness through significant technology transfiguration in line with customer expectations and regulations resulting in gratifying commercial growth in electrification. The industry now inspirited the next paradigm shift through Software Defined Vehicle concept with a strong conviction which can be understood as a ramification of the earlier success. Industry has now evolved from ECU-based architecture to Domain-based architecture and Model-Based Design has played a significant role in it. Now with the move to Zonal architecture and Service-Oriented Architecture, the paper focuses on the legacy battery charging system software monolith model, revamping it into a Service-oriented architecture compatible with Adaptive AUTOSAR framework within the native Model-Based Design Environment. The conversion involved transitioning from a signal-based architecture to an event and method-based architecture. Differences in detailed design and modelling styles are analyzed and addressed. Detailed design and modelling took place within the native MBD environment, followed by validation and verification of the integrated system. Code and executables were generated and validated for all the services and then integrated with the Linux operating system in a docker environment. The results demonstrated that while the legacy model-based design framework still has room for improvement, with careful design, legacy models can be converted to a service-oriented architecture without compromising their integrity and quality. The subsequent phase will involve integrating the code with a production-ready Adaptive AUTOSAR stack and conducting an analysis using an industry-qualified hardware platform.
